90727.e: Tiny living things in the water light up when the water moves. This is called sea sparkle.
90727.m: In sea sparkle, tiny living things in the water glow.

90728.q: What makes the light in the glowing lure of many anglerfish?
90728.e: Tiny bacteria that glow live in the lure. In return, the fish gives them a place to live.
90728.m: Glowing bacteria make the anglerfish's light.

90729.q: What colour is the light of many deep sea animals usually?
90729.e: Blue light travels furthest in water. That is why many deep sea animals glow blue.
90729.m: Many deep sea animals glow blue.

90730.q: Which deep sea fish is named after a lamp?
90730.e: Lanternfish have lots of small glowing spots on their bodies. They are among the most common fish in the deep sea.
90730.m: The lanternfish has glowing spots on its body.

90731.q: Why do many deep sea fish have a huge mouth?
a: They need a lot of air
90731.e: There is little to eat in the deep sea. With a big mouth they can grab any prey, even large prey.
90731.m: Deep sea fish often have a big mouth.

90732.q: Which animal on land also makes its own light?
90732.e: Like deep sea fish, glow-worms make their own light. You can see them glowing on summer nights.
90732.m: Glow-worms make their own light too.

90733.q: According to Swiss advice, how often at most should you eat meat?
90733.e: The Swiss dietary guidelines advise eating meat and sausage at most 2 to 3 times a week. On the other days you can have eggs, fish or tofu, for example.
90733.m: Meat is eaten only a few times a week.

90734.q: What is at the very top of the food pyramid?
90734.e: The top is very narrow. Sweet things and salty snacks should only be eaten rarely and in small amounts.
90734.m: The top of the pyramid shows what you should eat only rarely.

90735.q: Why is the food pyramid so wide at the bottom?
a: You should eat most of that
You should eat least of that
That is where the most expensive food is
90735.e: The wider a level is, the more of it you should eat or drink. At the top the pyramid gets narrow; that is where the things you need only a little of are.
90735.m: Wide levels mean a lot, narrow levels mean a little.

90736.q: How many portions of cereals or potatoes does the Swiss pyramid recommend per day?
90736.e: The Swiss dietary guidelines advise 3 portions a day from this group, for example bread, pasta, rice or potatoes.
90736.m: Three portions of cereals or potatoes a day give you energy.

90737.q: How many portions of dairy products does the Swiss food pyramid recommend per day?
90737.e: 2 to 3 portions of milk or dairy products a day are recommended. One portion is, for example, a glass of milk or a yoghurt.
90737.m: Two to three portions of dairy products a day are enough.

90738.q: Which group is directly above drinks in the food pyramid?
90738.e: Just above the drinks comes the second wide level with vegetables and fruit. So you should eat a lot of them.
90738.m: Vegetables and fruit are near the bottom of the pyramid.

90739.q: Which vegetable oil do the Swiss dietary guidelines especially recommend?
90739.e: The guidelines advise at least one tablespoon of rapeseed oil a day. Rapeseed is also grown in Switzerland.
90739.m: Rapeseed oil is a healthy cooking oil.

90740.q: How many tablespoons of vegetable oil does the Swiss pyramid recommend per day?
90740.e: About 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil a day are recommended, for example rapeseed oil for salad. The body needs oil in small amounts.
90740.m: A little vegetable oil every day is healthy.

90741.q: How many portions of meat, fish, eggs or tofu does the Swiss pyramid recommend per day?
90741.e: 1 portion of a protein-rich food a day is recommended. You should vary it.
90741.m: One portion of protein a day is enough.

90742.q: Which of these foods is a vegetable?
90742.e: The cucumber is a vegetable. Apples, pears and grapes are fruit.

90743.q: Which vegetable is orange and grows in the ground?
90743.e: The carrot is the orange root of the plant and grows underground. In Switzerland it is also called Rüebli.
90743.m: The carrot grows in the ground as an orange root.

90744.q: Which vegetable often makes your eyes water when you cut it?
90744.e: When you cut an onion, a substance is released that stings the eyes. That is why your eyes water.

90745.q: Which green vegetable looks like little trees?
90745.e: Broccoli has lots of small green florets on thick stalks. That is why it looks like little trees.
90745.m: Broccoli looks like a little forest.

90746.q: What colour is a ripe tomato usually?
90746.e: Ripe tomatoes are usually red. But there are also yellow and green varieties.

90747.q: What is lamb's lettuce, called Nüsslisalat in Switzerland?
a: A salad with small green leaves
90747.e: Lamb's lettuce has small dark green leaves and also grows in winter. Its Swiss name contains the word for nut, but it has nothing to do with nuts; it just tastes a little nutty.
90747.m: Lamb's lettuce is a salad with small leaves.

90748.q: Which vegetable is dark red and stains your hands when you cut it?
90748.e: Beetroot has a strong red colouring. It stains your hands and the chopping board red.

90749.q: Which vegetable is sauerkraut made from?
90749.e: Sauerkraut is made from finely shredded white cabbage that turns sour with salt. In Switzerland white cabbage is also called Kabis.
90749.m: Sauerkraut is made from white cabbage.

90750.q: Which fruit is yellow and curved?
90750.e: The banana has a yellow skin and is curved. It grows in warm countries.
90750.m: The banana is yellow and curved.

90751.q: Because of its many fruit trees, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”). Which fruit grows there especially often?
90751.e: There are very many apple trees in Thurgau. A lot of apple juice and cider is made from the apples there.
90751.m: Thurgau is known for its apples.

90752.q: Which fruit is a citrus fruit?
90752.e: Like the lemon and the mandarin, the orange is a citrus fruit. It has a lot of vitamin C.
90752.m: The orange is a citrus fruit.

90753.q: Which small red fruit has a hard stone in the middle?
90753.e: The cherry is a stone fruit. In the middle there is a hard stone that you don't eat.
90753.m: The cherry has a hard stone.

90754.q: Which fruit is brown and hairy outside and green inside?
90754.e: The kiwi has a brown, hairy skin. Inside it is green with lots of tiny black seeds.
90754.m: The kiwi is brown outside and green inside.

90755.q: Which small blue berry grows on low bushes in the woods?
90755.e: Bilberries grow on low bushes, including in Swiss woods. They are also called wild blueberries.

90756.q: Why should you wash fruit before eating it?
90756.e: There can be soil, dust and sprays on the skin. You wash them off with water.
90756.m: Wash fruit before you eat it.

90757.q: When are there fresh strawberries from the fields in Switzerland?
90757.e: Swiss strawberries are mainly picked in May, June and July. None grow outdoors in winter.
90757.m: Strawberries from the fields come in early summer.

90758.q: What is wholemeal bread made from?
90758.e: For wholemeal flour, the whole grain is ground, including the outer layer and the germ. Wholemeal bread is baked from it.
90758.m: Wholemeal bread contains the whole grain.

90759.q: What does wholemeal bread have more of than white bread?
90759.e: Wholemeal bread contains a lot of fibre. It is good for digestion.
90759.m: Wholemeal bread has a lot of fibre.

90760.q: Which ancient grain is related to wheat and popular in Switzerland for making bread?
90760.e: Spelt is an ancient kind of wheat. It has been grown in Switzerland for a long time and baked into bread.
90760.m: Spelt is an ancient bread grain.

90761.q: What colour is wholemeal bread usually?
90761.e: Because the dark outer layer of the grain is ground in too, wholemeal bread is usually brown.

90762.q: Which grain is most bread in Switzerland baked from?
90762.e: In Switzerland wheat is the most important bread grain. Wheat flour is used, for example, to bake Zopf plaited bread and Weggli rolls.
90762.m: Wheat is Switzerland's most important bread grain.

90763.q: Which parts of the grain are missing from white flour?
a: The outer layer and the germ
90763.e: For white flour, only the light-coloured inside of the grain is ground. The outer layer and the germ are removed.
90763.m: White flour has no outer layer and no germ.

90764.q: Which group of the food pyramid does wholemeal bread belong to?
90764.e: Bread is made from cereal grains. It belongs to the group with cereal products and potatoes.

90765.q: According to the guidelines, how many of the daily cereal portions should be wholegrain?
90765.e: The Swiss dietary guidelines advise eating at least half of your cereal products as wholegrain.
90765.m: At least half of your cereals should be wholegrain.

90766.q: Which of these foods is a dairy product?
90766.e: Quark is made from milk. Rice, honey and bread don't have milk as their main ingredient.

90767.q: What is the yellowish liquid left over when cheese is made called?
90767.e: When cheese is made, the milk separates into solid curds and liquid whey. The whey is often fed to pigs or made into drinks.
90767.m: Whey is left over when cheese is made.

90768.q: Which animal does most milk in Switzerland come from?
90768.e: Almost all the milk in Switzerland comes from cows. But there is also goat's and sheep's milk.
90768.m: Most milk in Switzerland comes from cows.

90769.q: Which well-known Swiss cheese has big holes?
90769.e: Emmentaler is famous for its big round holes. It comes from the Emmental valley in the canton of Bern.

90770.q: What do you get if you whip cream for a very long time?
90770.e: First the cream becomes whipped cream. If you keep going, the fat separates and you get butter.
90770.m: Cream whipped for a long time turns into butter.

90772.q: Which Swiss cheese dish is eaten from a shared pot?
90772.e: For fondue, cheese is melted in a special pot called a caquelon. Everyone dips their bread on a fork into the shared pot.
90772.m: Fondue is eaten together from one pot.

90773.q: Where do you keep an opened carton of milk?
90773.e: Milk stays fresh for longer in the fridge. In the warmth it soon goes sour.
90773.m: Opened milk belongs in the fridge.

90774.q: What should you do after eating sweets?
90774.e: After brushing your teeth, fewer bits of sugar stay on them. That keeps your teeth healthy.
90774.m: After sweet things it is best to brush your teeth.

90775.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
90775.e: In Switzerland sugar is made from sugar beet, for example in the factories in Aarberg and Frauenfeld.
90775.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

90776.q: How many sweet things per day does the Swiss food pyramid recommend at most?
90776.e: Sweet things are in the narrow top. You can enjoy them, but at most one small portion a day.
90776.m: Sweet things are allowed, but only a little.

90777.q: Which sweet food do bees make?
90777.e: Bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey. Honey contains a lot of sugar.

90778.q: What are the white, airy bakes made of egg white and sugar, which people in Switzerland like to eat with cream?
90778.e: Meringues are baked from whipped egg white and sugar. They are especially well known in the Bernese Oberland.
90778.m: Meringues are made of egg white and sugar.

90779.q: Which biscuit is a famous sweet treat from Basel?
90779.e: Basler Läckerli are small, hard gingerbread biscuits with honey and spices. They are a speciality of Basel.

90781.q: Which meal do you eat before the Znüni?
90781.e: First, in the morning, comes breakfast, called Zmorge in Swiss German. Later in the morning comes the Znüni.
90781.m: The Zmorge comes before the Znüni.

90783.q: Which fruit is especially easy to peel by hand for a mid-morning snack?
90783.e: You can peel a mandarin without a knife and split it into segments. That is why it is good for break time.
90783.m: A mandarin is a handy mid-morning snack.

90784.q: Why are crisps not a good mid-morning snack?
a: They have lots of fat and salt
90784.e: Crisps contain a lot of fat and salt but few vitamins. They don't keep you full for long.
90784.m: Crisps are not a good mid-morning snack.

90785.q: When do you usually eat your Znüni at school?
90785.e: Many schools have a long break in the morning. That is when the children eat their Znüni.
90785.m: The Znüni is eaten at morning break.

90786.q: Why is a mid-morning snack a good idea?
a: It gives energy for the morning
90786.e: It is a long time until lunch. A small snack helps you concentrate well.
90786.m: A mid-morning snack gives new energy for the morning.

90787.q: What is the best thing to bring your mid-morning snack to school in?
90787.e: In a snack box the food stays clean and does not get squashed. You can use the box again and again.
90787.m: A snack box protects your snack.

90788.q: Which vegetable is good to nibble raw as a mid-morning snack?
90788.e: Carrots can be eaten raw and are good to nibble. Raw potatoes are not eaten.
90788.m: Carrots make a tasty snack to nibble.

90789.q: What is a classic Swiss Zvieri?
a: Bread and a piece of chocolate
90789.e: A piece of bread with a little chocolate is a typical Zvieri in Switzerland. Rösti, fondue and raclette are main meals.
90789.m: Bread and chocolate are a typical Zvieri.

90791.q: What makes a good healthy afternoon snack?
90791.e: Yoghurt with fruit gives energy and vitamins. Jelly sweets and lemonade have a lot of sugar.
90791.m: Yoghurt with fruit is a good afternoon snack.

90792.q: Why should the afternoon snack be fairly small?
a: So you are still hungry in the evening
90792.e: A small afternoon snack takes away the hunger in the afternoon. Then you still have an appetite for dinner.
90792.m: A small afternoon snack leaves room for dinner.

90793.q: Which meal comes after the Zvieri?
90793.e: After the Zvieri in the afternoon comes dinner in the evening, called Znacht in Swiss German.

90794.q: Which afternoon snack provides a lot of protein?
90794.e: Cheese is made from milk and contains a lot of protein. Squash, sweets and cucumbers have hardly any protein.

90795.q: Which afternoon snack is healthy and crunchy?
a: Vegetable sticks with a quark dip
90795.e: Vegetable sticks such as cucumber or pepper give you vitamins. With a quark dip they taste even better.
90795.m: Vegetable sticks make a crunchy afternoon snack.

90796.q: Lunch is at 12 o'clock and the Zvieri at 4 pm (16:00). How many hours are there in between?
90796.e: From 12:00 to 16:00 is 16 minus 12, which is 4 hours.
90796.m: There are a few hours between lunch and the Zvieri.

90797.q: Where does most drinking water in Switzerland come from?
90797.e: About four fifths of Swiss drinking water comes from springs and groundwater. The rest comes mainly from lakes.
90797.m: Most Swiss drinking water comes from the ground.

90798.q: How can you always have water with you when you are out?
90798.e: You can fill a water bottle with tap water at home and take it with you. That way you can always have a drink.
90798.m: Always take a water bottle with you.

90799.q: How much unsweetened drink does the Swiss pyramid recommend for adults per day?
90799.e: 1 to 2 litres of unsweetened drinks a day are recommended, ideally water. Children need a little less.
90799.m: Adults should drink 1 to 2 litres a day.

90800.q: What is water from a protected spring that is sold in bottles called?
90800.e: Mineral water comes from protected underground springs and contains minerals. It is filled into bottles.

90801.q: What is a sign that the body needs water?
90801.e: Thirst is a signal from the body. It shows that you should drink.
90801.m: Thirst shows that you should drink.

90802.q: Which is much cheaper in Switzerland: tap water or bottled water?
90802.e: A litre of tap water in Switzerland costs only a fraction of a centime. Bottled water is much more expensive.

90803.q: From which lake does the city of Zurich get a large part of its drinking water?
90803.e: Zurich's water supply takes most of its water from Lake Zurich and treats it.
90803.m: Zurich drinks water from Lake Zurich.

90804.q: Who brings drinking water to people's homes?
90804.e: The water supply, usually run by the municipality, collects the water, checks it and sends it through pipes to the houses.
90804.m: The water supply delivers our drinking water.

90805.q: Can you drink from public fountains in Swiss towns?
a: Yes, if there is no warning sign
90805.e: Most town fountains have drinking water. Where the water is not safe to drink, there is a sign saying “Not drinking water”.
90805.m: You can drink from fountains without a warning sign.

90806.q: Roughly how much sugar is in half a litre of cola?
90806.e: Half a litre of normal cola contains over 50 grams of sugar. That is more than 10 sugar cubes.
90806.m: Sweet drinks hide a lot of sugar.

90807.q: Which drink is a sweet drink?
90807.e: Lemonade contains a lot of added sugar. Water and unsweetened tea have no sugar.

90808.q: What is the tooth disease called that can be caused by lots of sugar?
90808.e: Tooth decay makes holes in the teeth. People who often have sweet drinks are more likely to get tooth decay.
90808.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

90809.q: What is a good alternative to sweet drinks?
a: Water with a slice of lemon
90809.e: A slice of lemon gives water flavour without much sugar. That keeps the drink healthy.
90809.m: Water with lemon is a tasty thirst-quencher.

90810.e: Squash is very sweet. Well diluted with water, a glass contains less sugar.

90811.e: Herbal tea without sugar or honey contains no sugar. Iced tea, lemonade and cola are sweetened.
90811.m: Unsweetened tea is a good thirst-quencher.

90812.q: Why are energy drinks not suitable for children?
a: They have lots of caffeine and sugar
90812.e: Energy drinks contain a lot of caffeine and sugar. This is not healthy for children; it can cause a racing heart and sleep problems, for example.
90812.m: Energy drinks are not for children.

90813.q: What makes the bubbles in many sweet drinks?
90813.e: Many sweet drinks contain carbon dioxide. It makes the fizzy bubbles.
90813.m: Carbon dioxide makes the bubbles in drinks.

90814.q: Do frozen vegetables count towards your “5 a day”?
90814.e: Frozen vegetables count too. They are frozen soon after harvest and keep many good nutrients.

90815.q: How many of the five daily portions should be vegetables?
90815.e: 3 portions of vegetables plus fruit are recommended. So vegetables should make up the bigger part.
90815.m: More vegetables than fruit is ideal.

90816.q: Roughly how big is one portion for “5 a day”?
90816.e: One portion is about a handful. Children have smaller hands, so their portions are smaller.
90816.m: One portion roughly fits in your own hand.

90817.q: Which is healthier: a whole apple or a glass of apple juice?
90817.e: The 2024 Swiss dietary guidelines focus on whole fruit. It has more fibre and keeps you full longer than juice.
90817.m: Whole fruit is better than juice.

90818.q: Why should you eat vegetables and fruit in lots of colours?
a: Each colour has different good substances
90818.e: Different colours show different plant substances and vitamins. If you eat lots of colours, you get lots of them.

90819.q: What is the best way to manage your “5 a day”?
a: Some vegetables or fruit with every meal
All at once in the evening
90819.e: If you eat some vegetables or fruit with every meal and with your mid-morning and afternoon snacks, five portions soon add up.
90819.m: Every meal should include some vegetables or fruit.

90820.q: Which mid-morning snack helps with your “5 a day”?
90820.e: Apple slices are a portion of fruit. Crisps, biscuits and jelly sweets don't count.
90820.m: Fruit as a mid-morning snack helps with your “5 a day”.

90821.q: Do potatoes count towards the five portions of vegetables and fruit?
90821.e: In the pyramid, potatoes belong to the group with bread, rice and pasta. That is why they don't count towards “5 a day”.
90821.m: Potatoes don't count towards “5 a day”.

90822.e: Lentils grow in small pods. That is why they are pulses.

90823.q: What do peas grow in on the plant?
90823.e: Peas grow in green pods. Inside, the peas lie in a row.

90824.q: Which pulse is the main ingredient of hummus?
90824.e: Hummus is a paste made from cooked chickpeas. It comes from the Middle East.

90825.q: What do pulses contain especially a lot of?
90825.e: Pulses have a lot of protein and fibre. That is why they can replace meat.
90825.m: Pulses provide a lot of protein.

90826.e: Lentils are pulses. They make lentil soup hearty and keep you full for a long time.

90827.q: Do dried beans have to be cooked before you eat them?
90827.e: Raw beans contain substances that can give you tummy ache. Cooking destroys them.

90828.q: Which pulse is tofu made from?
90828.e: Tofu is made from soya milk, and soya milk from soya beans. Tofu originally comes from China.
90828.m: Tofu is made from soya beans.

90829.q: Which pulse goes into chilli con carne?
90829.e: Chilli con carne has red kidney beans in it. It also has minced meat, tomatoes and chilli.

90830.q: Which pulse is small, round and green?
90830.e: Peas are small, round, green balls. They are often eaten together with carrots.
90830.m: Peas are small, round and green.

90831.q: In German music notation, which note name comes after A?
90831.e: In German, the notes are called C, D, E, F, G, A and then H. In English this note is called B.
90831.m: In German, H comes after A.

90832.q: How many different natural notes are there from C to B?
90832.e: The natural notes are C, D, E, F, G, A and B. That is seven notes, and then it starts again with C.

90833.q: What is a row of notes that gets higher step by step called?
90833.e: A scale goes up or down step by step, like a ladder.
90833.m: A scale goes step by step.

90834.q: What is the difference between a musical note and a noise?
a: A note has a clear pitch
90834.e: You can sing a note because it has a definite pitch. A noise such as rustling has no clear pitch.
90834.m: A note has a definite pitch, a noise does not.

90835.q: What is the sign called that you use to write down a note?
90835.e: Music is written down with notes. The position of the note on the stave shows which note is meant.
90835.m: You write down sounds with notes.

90836.q: What is the distance from one C to the next higher C called?
90836.e: The octave is the distance between two notes with the same name. The higher one sounds very similar, just brighter.
90836.m: Two notes with the same name are an octave apart.
